definition: A degenerative process where a model trained repeatedly on data generated by earlier AI models (rather than diverse human-generated data) loses diversity and quality over successive generations.
details: Model collapse is a growing concern as more AI-generated content appears on the web and potentially gets swept into future training datasets, motivating interest in provenance tracking and careful data curation.
story: Imagine a new medicine that works brilliantly in the lab but still has to be tested on real people before anyone takes it. In plain words: A degenerative process where a model trained repeatedly on data generated by earlier AI models (rather than diverse human-generated data) loses diversity and quality over successive generations. Here is how it actually plays out: Model collapse is a growing concern as more AI-generated content appears on the web and potentially gets swept into future training datasets, motivating interest in provenance tracking and careful data curation. Rules and red-teaming are the brakes that make the speed trustworthy. That deliberate caution is Model Collapse.
